exposure: Single post-caesarean lower segment uterine scar
Grand multiparous women (parity ≥5) with single post-caesarean lower segment uterine scar
Grand multiparous women without scar uterus
cohort: Grand multiparous women (parity ≥5) with single post-caesarean lower segment uterine scar admitted at a gestational age of 37 completed weeks and above
finding: Grand multiparous women with single post-cesarean uterine scar have a comparable rate of vaginal delivery to those without a scar, and their Apgar scores at five minutes were better, suggesting they should be given a chance of vaginal delivery in the absence of added feto-maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: The frequency of vaginal delivery was slightly lower in grand multiparous women with a single uterine scar (75.8%) compared to those without a scar (87.5%), but this difference was not statistically significant.
